title.en: How the Printing Press Changed the World

label.en: How the Printing Press Changed the World

display.en: Today: How the Printing Press Changed the World.

spoken.en: Today: How the Printing Press Changed the World.

display.en: Before the 1450s, every book in Europe was copied by hand. A single Bible could take a scribe more than a year, so books were rare, expensive and mostly locked away in monasteries and universities.

spoken.en: Before the fourteen fifties, every book in Europe was copied by hand. A single Bible could take a scribe more than a year, so books were rare, expensive and mostly locked away in monasteries and universities.

display.en: Part 1: One machine, one idea.

spoken.en: Part one: One machine, one idea.

display.en: Around 1450, Johannes Gutenberg, a goldsmith in the German city of Mainz, combined several older inventions into one machine. He cast small metal letters that could be arranged, inked and pressed onto paper, then taken apart and used again.

spoken.en: Around fourteen fifty, Johannes Gutenberg, a goldsmith in the German city of Mainz, combined several older inventions into one machine. He cast small metal letters that could be arranged, inked and pressed onto paper, then taken apart and used again.

display.en: Movable type was not new, but his hard-wearing metal letters, oil-based ink and a press adapted from wine making made printing fast and cheap.

spoken.en: Movable type was not new, but his hard-wearing metal letters, oil-based ink and a press adapted from wine making made printing fast and cheap.

display.en: His workshop printed about 180 copies of the Bible around 1455. A team of printers could now do in weeks what scribes needed years to finish.

spoken.en: His workshop printed about one hundred eighty copies of the Bible around fourteen fifty-five. A team of printers could now do in weeks what scribes needed years to finish.

display.en: Key takeaway: His workshop printed about 180 copies of the Bible around 1455.

spoken.en: Key takeaway: His workshop printed about one hundred eighty copies of the Bible around fourteen fifty-five.

display.en: Part 2: Books everywhere.

spoken.en: Part two: Books everywhere.

display.en: The idea spread quickly. By 1500, printing presses were running in more than 250 European cities, and they had produced something like 20 million books. Prices fell, and for the first time ordinary merchants and craftsmen could own a book.

spoken.en: The idea spread quickly. By fifteen hundred, printing presses were running in more than two hundred fifty European cities, and they had produced something like twenty million books. Prices fell, and for the first time ordinary merchants and craftsmen could own a book.

display.en: More books meant more readers. Schools taught reading to more children, and people started to write in their own languages instead of Latin.

spoken.en: More books meant more readers. Schools taught reading to more children, and people started to write in their own languages instead of Latin.

display.en: Key takeaway: More books meant more readers.

spoken.en: Key takeaway: More books meant more readers.

display.en: Part 3: Ideas travel faster.

spoken.en: Part three: Ideas travel faster.

display.en: Printing did not just copy old books. It let new ideas move faster than any messenger. In 1517, Martin Luther's arguments against the church spread across Germany in a matter of weeks, because printers turned them into cheap pamphlets.

spoken.en: Printing did not just copy old books. It let new ideas move faster than any messenger. In fifteen seventeen, Martin Luther's arguments against the church spread across Germany in a matter of weeks, because printers turned them into cheap pamphlets.

display.en: Scientists benefited too. When astronomers and doctors could print their observations, other scholars could check them, argue with them and build on them. Many historians see this as one of the foundations of the scientific revolution.

spoken.en: Scientists benefited too. When astronomers and doctors could print their observations, other scholars could check them, argue with them and build on them. Many historians see this as one of the foundations of the scientific revolution.

display.en: Key takeaway: Many historians see this as one of the foundations of the scientific revolution.

spoken.en: Key takeaway: Many historians see this as one of the foundations of the scientific revolution.

headline.en: Many historians see this as one of the foundations of the scientific revolution.

display.en: The printing press turned knowledge from something scarce into something that could be shared. Every time you read a book, a newspaper or a website, you are using an idea that took off in a small workshop more than 570 years ago.

spoken.en: The printing press turned knowledge from something scarce into something that could be shared. Every time you read a book, a newspaper or a website, you are using an idea that took off in a small workshop more than five hundred seventy years ago.
